comparisons.peer_topic: Redemption Rights and Depositary Share Structures
comparisons.peer_summary: The Corporation may redeem most preferred stock series at its option at liquidation preference plus unpaid dividends, except for Series B and Series L which lack early redemption rights. Ownership is generally held via depositary shares representing fractional interests in preferred stock, with dividend payment frequencies and minimum rates varying by series as detailed in the table footnotes.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and Bank of America disclose that certain preferred stock series are issued as depositary shares representing fractional interests. Citi's Series Y uses a 1/25th interest structure with quarterly dividends until a 2026 reset date (c_2024_8_P612_S001, c_2024_8_P612_S002). BAC similarly notes depositary shares for various series, including 1/25th interests (bac_2024_8_P393_S001, bac_2024_8_P394_S001). However, Citi's Series Y has a specific fixed-to-floating reset mechanism tied to the five-year treasury rate plus 3.000%, whereas BAC's disclosed series have varying structures, with some lacking early redemption rights (Series B and L) and others having redemption rights at liquidation preference (bac_2024_8_P389_S001).

sentences.text: (10)Issued as depositary shares, each representing a 1/25th interest in a share of the corresponding series of non-cumulative perpetual preferred stock.

Dividends are payable quarterly on February 15, May 15, August 15 and November 15 at a fixed rate until, but excluding, November 15, 2026, thereafter payable quarterly on the same dates at a fixed rate that resets on the Series Y reset date and every five years thereafter equal to the five-year treasury rate plus 3.000%, in each case when, as and if declared by the Citi Board of Directors.

(6)Ownership is held in the form of depositary shares, each representing a 1/25th interest in a share of preferred stock, paying a semi-annual cash dividend, if and when declared, until the first redemption date at which time, it adjusts to a quarterly cash dividend, if and when declared, thereafter.
(7)Ownership is held in the form of depositary shares, each representing a 1/25th interest in a share of preferred stock, paying a quarterly cash dividend, if and when declared.
(2)The Corporation may redeem series of preferred stock on or after the redemption date, in whole or in part, at its option, at the liquidation preference plus declared and unpaid dividends.

comparisons.peer_topic: 2025 Issuance of Series Z Preferred Stock
comparisons.peer_summary: In January 2025, the firm issued 76,000 shares of Series Z 6.85% Fixed-Rate Reset Non-Cumulative Preferred Stock, which has a $25,000 liquidation preference, is redeemable at the firm's option starting February 10, 2030, and pays semi-annual dividends at 6.85% per annum until that date, thereafter resetting to 2.461% plus the five-year treasury rate.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi's Series Y and Goldman Sachs' Series Z employ a fixed-to-floating dividend reset structure tied to the five-year treasury rate. Citi's Series Y resets every five years to the five-year treasury rate plus 3.000% after November 15, 2026 (c_2024_8_P612_S002). Similarly, Goldman Sachs' Series Z, issued in January 2025, resets after February 10, 2030, to a rate equal to 2.461% plus the five-year treasury rate (gs_2024_8_P544_S003). Both series are non-cumulative and payable if declared.

sentences.text: Dividends are payable quarterly on February 15, May 15, August 15 and November 15 at a fixed rate until, but excluding, November 15, 2026, thereafter payable quarterly on the same dates at a fixed rate that resets on the Series Y reset date and every five years thereafter equal to the five-year treasury rate plus 3.000%, in each case when, as and if declared by the Citi Board of Directors.

Each share of Series Z Preferred Stock issued and outstanding has a liquidation preference of $25,000 per share, is represented by 25 depositary shares and is redeemable at the firm's option beginning February 10, 2030 at a redemption price equal to $25,000 per share plus declared and unpaid dividends.

Dividends on Series Z Preferred Stock, if declared, are payable semi-annually at (i) 6.85% per annum from the issuance date to, but excluding, February 10, 2030 and, thereafter, (ii) 2.461% per annum plus the five-year treasury rate.

comparisons.peer_topic: Preferred Stock Dividend Policy and Reference Rates
comparisons.peer_summary: Dividends are discretionary, non-cumulative, and declared quarterly. Fixed-to-floating rate preferred stock uses SOFR or CMT as reference rates following the transition from LIBOR, with specific spread adjustments defined.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and JPMorgan disclose preferred stock terms involving fixed-to-floating rate resets and dividend payment frequencies. Citi's Series Y pays quarterly dividends at a fixed rate until 2026, then resets to a floating rate based on the five-year treasury rate plus 3.000% (c_2024_8_P612_S002). JPMorgan's preferred stock also utilizes fixed-to-floating structures, with reference rates transitioning from LIBOR to SOFR or CMT (five-year Constant Maturity Treasury rate) plus spreads, and dividends payable quarterly after conversion to a floating rate (jpm_2024_8_P749_S001, jpm_2024_8_P749_S003, jpm_2024_8_P750_S004).

sentences.text: Dividends are payable quarterly on February 15, May 15, August 15 and November 15 at a fixed rate until, but excluding, November 15, 2026, thereafter payable quarterly on the same dates at a fixed rate that resets on the Series Y reset date and every five years thereafter equal to the five-year treasury rate plus 3.000%, in each case when, as and if declared by the Citi Board of Directors.
(c)Effective June 30, 2023, CME Term SOFR became the replacement reference rate for fixed-to-floating rate preferred stock issued by the Firm that formerly referenced U.S. dollar LIBOR.
References to "CMT" mean a floating annualized rate equal to the five-year Constant Maturity Treasury ("CMT") rate plus the spreads noted.
Dividends are payable semiannually on fixed-to-floating rate preferred stock while at a fixed rate, and payable quarterly after converting to a floating rate.

comparisons.peer_summary: Series M preferred stock dividends are payable semiannually until September 15, 2026, and quarterly thereafter.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi's Series Y and Morgan Stanley's Series M feature preferred stock dividends that start at a fixed rate and transition to a more frequent payment schedule (or potentially floating rate structure) after a specific date. Citi's Series Y pays quarterly fixed dividends until November 15, 2026, and continues quarterly thereafter with a rate reset (c_2024_8_P612_S002). Morgan Stanley's Series M pays semiannually until September 15, 2026, and then becomes payable quarterly (ms_2024_8_P507_S001). Both use 2026 as a key date for structural change in dividend payment frequency.
